plan.focus: Field-level evidence of indoor heat exposure and physical access barriers among vulnerable urban residents, alongside audited operational metrics and measured health outcomes from municipal cooling center activations.
plan.reason: Prior discovery retrieved generic policy guidance and regional epidemiological models rather than direct documentation of resident-level access constraints or empirical audits of municipal heat action plan operations. Targeted searches must isolate field surveys of vulnerable populations and official operational post-incident reviews.
hypotheses: Practical barriers such as lack of transit, limited operating hours, and security concerns depress cooling center attendance among older adults and low-income residents despite high indoor heat exposure.

Municipal heat emergency post-incident audits document supply-side outputs like facility openings and water distribution, but rarely measure changes in heat-related morbidity or reach among unhoused and isolated residents.
Empirical assessments of heat action plans reveal that health improvements depend more on direct residential cooling subsidies and outreach than on passive cooling center activation.
